label: Sketch, then cut
subgoals: Cut the graph at the boundary value
Shade the arc satisfying the inequality

slice.rule: To solve a trigonometric inequality, sketch the relevant function over one $2\pi$ period, draw the horizontal (or sloped) line for the boundary value, and read off the arcs where the graph sits on the required side. Testing one point inside each candidate arc confirms it, which is cheaper than solving algebraically.

examples.says: keep the arcs where the curve rises above the line $y=k$
keep the arcs where the curve falls left of the line $x=k$

label: Shade, then transfer
subgoals: Test one point inside each candidate arc

slice.rule: The shaded arcs on the unit circle are the same arcs: read the sign of the function off the unit-circle position, and each solution arc transfers directly into interval form.

examples.says: the arcs where the unit-circle ray lies above the line $y=kx$

label: Close the answer
subgoals: Intersect solution arcs with the given domain
Union disjoint arcs into the final set

slice.rule: A trigonometric solution on all reals repeats: add $2k\pi$ for every integer $k$. Then intersect with whatever domain the problem gave, drop endpoints that fail a strict inequality, and union the surviving disjoint arcs into the final set.
slice.note: Intersecting with the domain after writing the general solution is the step most often forgotten.
